stimuli.description: Four distinct physical environments: two natural bamboo forests (YA, YB), one bamboo forest park (DJY), and one urban environment (CS). Participants viewed the landscape and walked in these areas.

tables.description: Basic information of the sampling subjects at the four sites included in this study, including age, weight, height, BMI, SBP, DBP, HR, and SpO2 for male and female participants in each group.
Comparison of environmental factors (Temperature, Relative humidity, Radiant heat, Noise, Absolute illumination, Wind velocity, Negative oxygen ion concentration) across the four experimental sites.
key_stats: Temperature: YB (23.2 ± 0.5 °C, p<0.05 vs CS), DJY (18.7 ± 0.5 °C, p<0.01 vs CS)
Relative humidity: CS (60.5 ± 2.53 %, p<0.05 vs YA)
Radiant heat: YA (26.3 ± 0.3 °C, p<0.05 vs CS), YB (26.2 ± 1.0 °C, p<0.05 vs CS), DJY (17.8 ± 0.3 °C, p<0.01 vs CS)
Absolute illumination: YA (877.1 ± 337.0 lx, p<0.01 vs CS), YB (3774.7 ± 583.0 lx, p<0.05 vs CS), DJY (815.2 ± 267.0 lx, p<0.01 vs CS)
Wind velocity: YA (0.1 ± 0.1 m/s, p<0.05 vs CS), YB (0.2 ± 0.1 m/s, p<0.05 vs CS)

tables.description: Results of principal component analysis showing factor loads for 25 semantic differential evaluation items across 5 extracted factors (Sensory, Atmosphere, Climate, Place, Space).
Comprehensive evaluation scores (F scores) for the five environmental characteristic factors (F1-F5) and an overall F score for each of the four experimental sites.
key_stats: Overall F score: YB (1.01), YA (0.96), DJY (0.92), CS (0.09)

limitations: The study was only carried out in the summer, limiting generalizability to other seasons.
Subjects were all university students from Sichuan Agricultural University, which may limit generalizability to other populations with different occupations, age groups, and life backgrounds.
The study evaluated only physiological indicators; future research should include psychological and endocrine hormones for a more comprehensive reflection of environmental impact on health.
